chunk: Termination & Exit Policy (EN, 202501) # Termination & Exit Policy Company: Global Service Firm Version: 202501 Region: Global (EN)

The purpose of this Termination & Exit Policy is to outline the procedures and guidelines governing the termination of employment at Global Service Firm. This policy applies to all employees across all regions and aims to ensure a fair, transparent, and respectful process for both employees and the organization. It covers various forms of termination, including voluntary resignations, retirements, redundancies, dismissals, and mutual agreements.

Voluntary Resignation: The act of an employee choosing to leave the company of their own accord. Retirement: The voluntary departure of an employee from the workforce, typically upon reaching a certain age or after a designated period of service. Redundancy: Termination of employment due to the position being no longer needed, often as a result of organizational changes or economic conditions. Dismissal: Termination initiated by the employer for reasons related to the employee's performance or behavior. Termination for Cause: Dismissal due to serious misconduct or failure to meet job expectations. Mutual Agreement: A situation where both the employer and employee agree to end the employment relationship under specific terms.

1. Fairness: All terminations will be conducted fairly and without bias. 2. Compliance: Adherence to local laws and regulations is paramount. 3. Dignity: Employees will be treated with respect throughout the termination process. 4. Documentation: All decisions and communications will be documented to ensure clarity and accountability. 5. Transparency: Clear communication will be maintained with employees regarding the reasons for termination.

Standard Durations: Employees are generally required to provide a notice period of two weeks to one month, depending on their role and length of service. Regional Variations: Notice periods may vary by region; local laws will be taken into account. Waivers: In certain circumstances, notice periods may be waived by mutual agreement.

1. Employee Notification: Employees must submit their resignation in writing to their immediate supervisor. 2. HR Confirmation: HR will acknowledge receipt of the resignation and confirm the last working day. 3. Exit Interview Scheduling: HR will schedule an exit interview to gather feedback and insights.
Employees will be informed of the redundancy situation and provided with options, including potential redeployment.
Employees will receive feedback and support to improve performance before termination is considered.
Investigations will be conducted to ensure fair treatment before any dismissal for misconduct.
Employees affected by restructuring will be notified in advance and provided with options for transition.

section: Role of HR and Line Managers
chunk: HR: Responsible for overseeing the termination process, ensuring compliance with policies, and conducting exit interviews. Line Managers: Responsible for communicating performance issues or organizational changes and supporting employees through the transition.
Gather feedback on the employee's experience within the organization. Identify areas for improvement in workplace culture and processes.
What prompted your decision to leave? Were your job expectations met? What could have been done differently?
All information shared during the exit interview will be treated as confidential.
HR will compile insights from exit interviews to inform organizational improvements.

Employees must return all company property, including laptops, phones, and access cards, prior to their last working day. Access to company systems will be revoked on the last day of employment. IT offboarding will be conducted to ensure data security.
Employees will receive their final paycheck, including any accrued leave, on the next scheduled pay date. Benefits will be reviewed, and employees will be informed of any continuation or termination.
Employees may request a reference letter or employment certificate, which will be provided upon request.

Probationary Employees: Different notice periods may apply. Executives: Termination processes may involve additional considerations and agreements. CrossBorder Contracts: Local laws will dictate the termination process.
Employees are reminded of their obligations regarding nondisclosure, noncompete clauses, and conflict of interest.
Employees who feel their termination was unjust may escalate their grievance to HR or higher management.
All documentation related to terminations will be maintained in accordance with legal requirements and company policy.
This policy will be reviewed annually to ensure compliance and relevance. Changes will be communicated to all employees.

#### Case Study 1: Voluntary Resignation An employee in the marketing department submitted a resignation letter due to personal reasons. HR facilitated an exit interview, gathering valuable feedback on team dynamics. The employee returned company property and received a positive reference. #### Case Study 2: Redundancy Due to a restructuring initiative, several positions in the finance department were made redundant. Affected employees were offered redeployment options and severance packages. HR conducted individual meetings to discuss the changes and support available. #### Case Study 3: Dismissal for Misconduct An employee was dismissed for repeated violations of company policy. HR conducted a thorough investigation, documenting each step. The employee was informed of the decision and provided with a final paycheck. #### Case Study 4: Executive Exit An executive decided to leave the company for personal reasons. HR worked closely with the executive to ensure a smooth transition, including knowledge transfer and communication to the team.

1. What should I do if I want to resign? Submit a written resignation to your manager. 2. How much notice do I need to give? Generally, two weeks to one month, depending on your role. 3. What happens during an exit interview? You'll discuss your experiences and provide feedback. 4. When will I receive my final paycheck? On the next scheduled pay date after your last working day. 5. Can I request a reference? Yes, you can request a reference letter from HR. 6. What if I feel my termination was unfair? You can escalate your grievance to HR. 7. What happens to my benefits after termination? HR will inform you about the continuation or termination of benefits. 8. Do I need to return company property? Yes, all company property must be returned. 9. What are my posttermination obligations? You must adhere to any nondisclosure or noncompete agreements. 10. How is the policy enforced? HR oversees compliance and documentation. 11. What if I have a crossborder contract? Local laws will dictate the termination process. 12. How often is this policy reviewed? Annually, or as needed.

subsection: Appendix: Global Benchmarks and Key Risks
chunk: Benchmarks: Companies with clear termination policies report higher employee satisfaction and lower turnover rates. Key Risks: Failure to follow this policy can lead to legal disputes, damage to the company’s reputation, and decreased employee morale. This Termination & Exit Policy is designed to ensure a smooth and respectful transition for employees leaving Global Service Firm. All employees are encouraged to familiarize themselves with this policy and reach out to HR with any questions.
